statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20%, at the floor of the watch band and below the 25% block threshold, while Stress stays high at 70% on long-end yields and crude.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at WATCH for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD alike. The overnight Globex tape has drifted slightly higher over the past hour, from plus 0.11% to plus 0.22%, but the entire band is only about 0.36% wide on roughly 7.4k contracts, and Micron's record fiscal Q4 still has not produced upside continuation. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at its own session low after a higher intraday print, which is retracement rather than extension. Long-end yields at multi-decade highs and crude near $90 keep Stress high at 70%, but neither has yet transmitted into a no-pullback NQ path. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:00 to 15:00 UTC on 1 October, where jobless claims, Fed commentary, the US cash open and ISM manufacturing stack inside three hours.
headline: Thin Globex drift lifts NQ to plus 0.22% while Micron's record quarter still fails to extend; Tail holds 20% at the watch-band floor
body: NQ futures last printed 30,767.00 at 19:16 ET on 30 September, up 68.25 points or 0.22% from the 30,698.75 settle, inside a 30,684.50 to 30,794.75 overnight band on roughly 7.4k contracts; Investing.com independently shows 30,770.50, up 0.23%, at the same minute. That is a mild, thin drift higher rather than a directional leg: the full band is about 0.36% wide, and although the high has extended from the 30,740.50 seen an hour earlier, volume remains negligible. Micron's record fiscal Q4 still has not extended into a one-way memory-led path. Revenue was $54.2 billion with adjusted EPS of $33.42 against $31.16 expected, and fiscal Q1 2027 guidance is $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion with adjusted EPS of $38.15 plus or minus $1.00, yet the shares slipped 0.78% after hours to $1,056.75 from a $1,066.10 close as investors weighed gross-margin guidance of about 86.25% against the 87.0% just delivered. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,408.50, up 0.23%, exactly at its session low after a 30,630.45 high, so the cash session faded into the bell; the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.24% to 26,861.06 while the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,651.54 and the Dow dropped 0.86% to 50,906.05. September finished with the Dow down 4.9%, the S&P 500 down 0.7% and the Nasdaq up 1.7%, a split that points to rotation rather than index-level one-way risk. VIX settled at 16.34, up 1.87%, inside a 15.62 to 16.61 range, so no volatility stress corroborates a pathological path. The dominant stress channel stays rates and energy. The latest H.15 column, dated 29 September, shows the 2-year at 4.89%, the 10-year at 5.26% and the 30-year at 5.59%, while 30 September trade lifted the 10-year to 5.29% after briefly breaching 5.30% and the 30-year to 5.62%, the highest since 2002. WTI trades near $90.12, up 0.82%, with Brent around $102.59 after a roughly 13% September gain. Geopolitically the Iran conflict remains active but is not a fresh discontinuity: Middle East crude exports reached an estimated 16.328 million barrels a day in September, the highest since the war began in February, with about 9.719 million a day moving through the Strait of Hormuz, even as projectiles struck three ships in the waterway on Tuesday. Taken together the evidence shows an orderly, thin, two-sided tape with a live rates and energy stress channel and no observed mean-reversion failure, so Tail holds at 20%, the floor of the watch band, with Stress at 70% and Confidence at 88%.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. Tail sat at 15-17% through the Asian and European hours of 30 September, stepped into the watch band from 12:00 UTC as the US session developed, peaked at 23% between 15:00 and 16:00 UTC and eased back to 20-22% across the cash close and the Globex reopen. Stress held between 65% and 72% throughout, Confidence between 85% and 88%, and the dominant mode was mixed for every slot except the first two.
outlookSummary: The projection eases out of the watch band for ten slots between 00:00 and 09:00 UTC on 1 October, reaching a 17% low through the orderly mid-Asia hours, on the assumption the contained overnight band holds. Conditional Tail re-enters the watch band at 10:00 UTC and peaks at 23% across 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, where Fed commentary, the US cash open and ISM manufacturing stack inside two hours; those slots are scored event/whipsaw because a two-sided reaction is the base case and sustained directional continuation would be the first genuine amplifier. Tail then decays through the US afternoon, ticks up once for the 19:00 UTC power hour, eases below the band again during the 21:00 UTC CME halt where no continuous price path can form, and returns to the 20% watch-band floor for the Globex reopen with Friday's payrolls still unresolved. Stress stays between 68% and 73% on long-end yields and crude, and Confidence drifts from 88% to 83% as the projection extends away from the verified 23:16 UTC futures print.
